blindSummary: Trans visitors here face a high level of documented risk. Common law criminalises same-sex intimacy; trans people have no access to legal gender recognition and healthcare options are limited; the country's absolute monarchy punishes dissent harshly (sedition laws; activists assassinated, per a 2024 governance report); LGBT people face documented discrimination. The national Pride event has proceeded annually since 2018 under heavy conditions — a small space of visibility.
blindOutOfScope: Repression associated with the monarchy is a general risk affecting everyone; Pride proceeds annually.
blindSourceSummaries: International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): common law criminalises consensual same-sex intimacy; no legal gender recognition and limited gender-affirming healthcare; intersex people lack safeguards; in April 2022 the high court rejected an LGBT organisation's bid for registration, but in June 2023 the supreme court declared the registrar's decision void; the commerce ministry still refuses registration, claiming the organisation's name and objectives 'seek to offend against customary principles'.

Freedom-watchdog annual assessment (2024): this country is rated 'not free' (17/100) - an absolute monarchy; political dissent harshly punished; discrimination against women and LGBT+ people among the human-rights problems.

Governance-index country report (2024) by a political foundation: the last absolute monarchy in its world region - the king and queen mother hold veto powers over all branches of government; governance and human-rights context.
A foreign government's 2021 human-rights report on this country: official assessment - sodomy laws (common law) remain; significant societal stigma; no legal protections for LGBT persons.

Media commentary site (Dec 2018): a church welcoming LGBTIQ people reopened in a residential area outside the capital; an activist at an LGBT advocacy organisation welcomed it while noting religious hate speech; a regional gender-rights report described a meeting where 20+ pastors called LGBTI behaviour 'demonic' and refused to let gay people 'flaunt' themselves.

Independent news site (July 2018): history made as the country's first Pride was declared a 'perfect' success - more than 2,000 people attended in the capital, with a police-escorted march around the main stadium; the organiser, an LGBT activist, was 'beyond thrilled'.

The same independent news site (July 2019): the country's registrar of companies refused to register the leading sexual- and gender-minorities organisation, calling its objectives a 'negative mindset' - other groups had to include 'acceptable' health/HIV aims to register; that organisation's first objective is to advance LGBT rights.
blindTangential: Common-law criminalisation of same-sex intimacy — formal exposure for visitors travelling with partners.
